ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, on a horizontal tabletop there are three identical objects a, b, and c stacked together. The left end of a is connected by a light rope to a small ball of mass m = 3kg. The angle between the rope and the horizontal direction is $60^{\circ}$. The small ball is at rest in a smooth semicircular vessel. A horizontally rightward force F = 40N acts on b, and the three objects remain in a stationary state. Take g as 10$m/s^2$. Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Object b is subjected to one frictional force, directed to the left

The left end of a is connected by a light rope to a small ball of mass m=3kg. The angle between the rope and the horizontal direction is 60°. The small ball is at rest in a smooth semicircular vessel. A horizontally rightward force F=40N acts on b, and the three objects remain in a stationary state. Take g as 10m/s^2. At this time, is object b subjected to a frictional force? If it is, what is its direction?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Object b is subjected to one frictional force, directed to the left
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure, three objects are stacked on a horizontal tabletop; the bottom layer is labeled a, the middle is labeled b, and the top layer is labeled c; a light rope extends horizontally leftward from the left end of a to connect to the small ball in the semicircular smooth vessel, and the rope is marked as making 60° with the horizontal direction; on the middle object b there is a horizontally rightward external force F. The three objects remain stationary. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take b and c as a whole to analyze the forces in the horizontal direction. The frictional force between b and c is an internal force of this whole and cannot change the horizontal resultant force of the whole. For the b+c whole, the external horizontal forces include the rightward force F acting on b, and the frictional force exerted by the lower object a on b. Since the b+c whole is stationary, the horizontal resultant force must be zero, so the frictional force exerted by a on b must be to the left to balance the rightward F. Therefore object b is subjected to a frictional force, and the direction of this frictional force is to the left.
